task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the replacement of a community fridge with staffed pantry sessions in Oatbridge. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Oatbridge Food Circle will close its outdoor community fridge Sept. 30, 2026, when permission to use the host property's forecourt ends.
The host business is renovating its entrance, and the circle has not described the closure as the result of a food-safety violation.
The circle will begin staffed pantry sessions at the neighborhood hall on Oct. 6, rather than moving the same fridge to another outdoor site.
The pantry will open Tuesday evenings and Saturday mornings; the outdoor fridge can currently be approached at any hour.
The hall has offered a lockable food-storage room under a one-year agreement, with renewal still to be negotiated.
An $18,600 community grant allocates $9,300 to a year's room charges and $9,300 to equipment, transport and volunteer training.
Visitors will not need a referral or proof of income to use the pantry under the circle's supplied participation policy.
Food availability will depend on donations and storage capacity, and the circle has not promised a fixed parcel for every visit.
Coordinator Una Fenn said, "We can offer a person to ask, but we are losing the freedom to come at three in the morning."
A group of shift workers asked the circle to assess access outside the two opening sessions before treating the new arrangement as a full replacement.
Resident representative Cal Roven said, "A staffed door can be welcoming and still be a closed door when your shift ends."
The circle will collect feedback during the first month before deciding whether it has enough volunteers for another session.
Four local food businesses will continue donating, but their written commitments do not specify a guaranteed daily quantity.
Donations will be received by volunteers during arranged delivery windows instead of being left anonymously on the hall doorstep.
The hall's other users will not have general access to the pantry's locked storage room.
Existing fridge notices will list the closure date, new opening sessions and the circle's contact point during the transition.
The circle has arranged a final collection of remaining food before the forecourt closes, using its existing donation-handling procedures.
The packet contains no estimate of how many distinct households used the unstaffed fridge.
The fridge door has carried handwritten recipe cards and spare shopping bags supplied by visitors.
Volunteers hope to retain the recipe-card exchange at the pantry, but recipe cards are not a condition of receiving food.
The new grant covers one year and does not establish a permanent municipal food service.
The circle says its new records will count visits and stock movements, not assess individual visitors' health or nutritional outcomes.

forbidden_additions: A food-safety shutdown, guaranteed food parcels or measured health benefits.
Round-the-clock pantry access or a permanent funded service.
A mandatory income test or unverified household-use count.
preserve: The gain in staffed assistance and the loss of unrestricted access.
The property-related reason for closure and the transition dates.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
